Maya: quick heads-up — seeing a perf regression on INT4 path on H100 when seq_len > 4096, reproducer and profiles below. cc @Raj @Luis
Raj: uh ok details? logs? what changed in last rollout?
Maya: rolled kernel_v3 for sm90 last night; compare runs: kernel_v2 (old) vs kernel_v3 (new) on same pinned model+quant.
Maya: ```
# microbench (single-stream, no batching)
model: rwkv-30b
quant: int4
hardware: H100 sm90
seq=512 batch=1 -> 0.42 ms/token (v2) -> 0.44 ms/token (v3)
seq=2048 batch=1 -> 0.85 ms/token (v2) -> 0.95 ms/token (v3)
seq=8192 batch=1 -> 1.78 ms/token (v2) -> 2.34 ms/token (v3)
# breakdown shows extra global memcopy + different kernel choice for matmul forward
```
Luis: interesting — looks like v3 picks a tiled int4 kernel that assumes 256x32 tiling which is great for short seqs but memory-copy overhead kills it at long seqs.
Jen: do we have per-arch heuristics that consider seq_len when selecting kernel? I thought selector keys on batch+model_size+quant only.
Maya: right now selector key: (arch_family, dtype, model_macs, batch_size). no seq buckets.
Raj: that explains it. Proposal: add seq_len buckets (e.g. <=512, 513-2048, 2049-8192, >8192) to autotuner lookup and store best kernel per bucket.
Raj: also add a KV-cache warmup heuristic: if running with persistent KV and seen >N tokens since cold start, allow kernel switch to high-throughput path.
PerfBot: perf alert created: alert/1979-int4-h100-seqlen-regression (sensitivity high)
Maya: attached flamegraph snippet (inline): extra copies happening in prepare_inputs -> transform_layout.
Luis: short checklist to fix: 1) add seq bucket key 2) update autotuner to record median latency per kernel per bucket 3) add hysteresis threshold (use 1.05 multiplier) to avoid flapping 4) KV warmup flag for long-lived sessions
Jen: hysteresis sounds good — do we prefer additive (ms) or multiplicative? For cross-arch multiplicative is more robust. propose multiplier=1.05 for selection, 1.02 for rollback safety margin.
Maya: also saw memory-pressure dependent fallback: on H100 with >24GB active KV, some kernels hit workspace allocation failure and fallback to a slower kernel. Need to record last-fallback-reason in profile so selector avoids choices that require extra workspace when free_mem < threshold.
Raj: agree. new selector key will include workspace_requirement_bucket: {low, medium, high} derived from kernel metadata.
Maya: prototype patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3892 — adds seq buckets and hysteresis logic. still needs tests and perf CI.
Maya: sample of autotuner entry format (stored in local cache):
```
key: sm90|int4|rwkv-30b|batch1|seq=2049-8192|workspace=high
best_kernel: kernel_v2
median_ms: 1.78
samples: 34
last_fallback_reason: workspace_alloc_failed
```
Raj: where do we persist the autotuner DB? local FS is fine but for Dedicated customers we should have option to persist to object storage and share across nodes.
Luis: yes. propose default location /var/lib/redwood/selector_profiles and optional S3 sync. Keep file-per-arch to limit lock contention.
InfraBot: note — persisting to S3 will require config flag and IAM role, track as infra task INF-723.
Jen: testing matrix — need to run for sm80/sm90/sm92/sm95, quant int8/int4/fp8, seq buckets, batch sizes 1..8. heavy matrix but we can sample sensible combos.
Maya: quick perf run suggestion: run local autotune harness with --seq-buckets "512,2048,8192" --quant int4 --arch sm90 --batch 1,2,4. output is JSON summary with median lat and workspace cost.
Luis: also add a small KV warmup bench: start cold, generate 100 tokens to fill cache, then measure long stream. If warmup_count > threshold (e.g., 128 tokens) allow high-throughput kernel paths.
Raj: one more edge: FP8 path on H100 uses tensorcore kernels with packing that assume 16-byte alignment. For odd batch sizes we lose perf; autotuner should record alignment sensitivity and prefer padded batching or different kernel.
Maya: ok I'll land the prototype patch for seq-buckets + hysteresis tomorrow, then run perf matrix on staging. posting results back here.
Jen: thanks — if you need extra runs I can queue on perf cluster.
Maya: thanks all. filing follow-ups: PR review, perf matrix runs, infra task for S3. :thumbsup:
